title: Mitä: classifying several things
focus: Ask what several things are and answer with a plural category: Mitä nämä ovat? Nämä ovat kirjoja.

exercises.prompt: Write “What are these?” in Finnish. Use nämä (“these”), ovat (“are”). Ask for a category.
exercises.explanation: Mitä nämä ovat? means “What are these?” Mitä asks for a category; the plural subject uses ovat and the category takes the supplied plural partitive.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking for the objects’ category + plural subject (the objects being classified) + verb

parts.role: question asking for the objects’ category
parts.formation: Mitä is the partitive form of mikä. With a plural subject and ovat, it asks for the category of the objects here; mitkä selects identifiable objects instead.
Nämä is the plural of tämä (“this”). It stands alone as the subject here and takes the plural verb ovat or eivät ole.
Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.

optionFeedback.Mitä nämä ovat?: Mitä nämä ovat? means “What are these?” Mitä asks for a category; the plural subject uses ovat and the category takes the supplied plural partitive.
optionFeedback.Mitkä nämä ovat?: Ask what category the objects belong to with mitä. Keep plural subject–verb agreement: nämä/nuo/ne ovat.
optionFeedback.Mikä nämä ovat?: A plural classification reply uses the supplied partitive-plural category, not a singular basic noun or singular mikä.
